$comment: Advisories consciously accepted by the 🔒 Security Audit gate. Every entry needs a reason and a reviewBy date; check-npm-audit.js fails once an entry expires or stops matching a live advisory, so exceptions cannot rot silently.

allow.title: extract-zip unvalidated symlink path traversal
allow.reason: No patched release exists — extract-zip 2.0.1 is still the latest published version. It reaches us only as a transitive devDependency through three paths, all via puppeteer-core/puppeteer 24.x -> @puppeteer/browsers 2.x: @lhci/cli 0.15.1 -> lighthouse 12.6.1, the direct lighthouse ^12.8.2, and pa11y-ci 4.1.1 -> puppeteer. @lhci/cli 0.15.1 is the latest release and hard-pins lighthouse to exactly 12.6.1, so that path has no forward upgrade (npm's remedy there is a downgrade to @lhci/cli 0.12.0). The other two paths have major upgrades (lighthouse 13.5.0, pa11y-ci 5.0.0, which also needs the puppeteer override moved to ^25), deferred as out of scope for a security-gate fix and pointless while the @lhci/cli path keeps extract-zip in the tree. The fix exists upstream — @puppeteer/browsers 3.x replaced extract-zip with modern-tar — so remove this entry once @lhci/cli picks up lighthouse 13.x. Exposure is limited to CI: package.json declares zero runtime dependencies, so none of this ships to readers, and the only archives these packages extract are Chrome builds fetched from Google's official download endpoints during test setup, not attacker-supplied zips.

allow.title: extract-zip allows arbitrary file writes through symlink archive entries
allow.reason: A second advisory against the same unpatched extract-zip 2.0.1 (range <=2.0.1) on the same three dependency paths as #1139346 above; that entry's reasoning and exposure apply unchanged. Remove both entries together once @lhci/cli consumes lighthouse 13.x (#1351).
